newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil slightly firmer, refiners buying.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil slightly firmer, refiners buying.

text.p: NWE gas oil prices were slightly firmer on Thursday with benchmark gas oil futures turning round Wednesday's losses and fairly good buying interest seen from refiners, traders said.

However, heating oil barges were only very slightly higher by late morning, futures having shed most of their early $2 gains. Offers for Rotterdam product remained at around IPE June +$1.50 fob Rotterdam, or 75 cents/+$1 fob Antwerp/Flushing.
Traders said fresh demand was coming from traders, rather than end-consumers, as buying appeared more profitable than producing 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil.
"There's not much sense producing marginal quantities of 0.2 material," one trader said.
The buying was focused mainly on cheaper Flushing material with trade seen at June IPE +50 and +75 cents a tonne for prompt liftings.

An EN590 barge traded at June IPE +10 cents fob ARA, around $1 down from Wednesday's values. 0.2 sulphur cargo premiums held steady. Russian cargoes valued around June IPE +$3 a tonne cif NWE after trade at +$2.75 on Wednesday.
EN590 cargoes held around June IPE +$11 a tonne following trade at the level into Le Havre.
